articles.title: Anger or fear? Dogs may be able to read it on your face
articles.snippet: Brain scans offer the first evidence that dogs can read certain human facial expressions.
articles.summary: Brain scans provide the first evidence that dogs can read certain human facial expressions. This shows that dogs might be able to tell the difference between emotions like anger or fear on your face.

articles.title: These clues might point to life on other worlds
articles.snippet: Gases and color on distant planets may trace to activity by extraterrestrial life. If so, those E.T.s are likely tiny, one-celled beings.
articles.summary: Scientists say that gases and colors on distant planets could be clues pointing to tiny, one-celled extraterrestrial life. These signs might mean that simple alien beings are active on other worlds.

articles.title: Some germs ride a superhighway at the edge of space
articles.snippet: Some microbes common on Earth’s surface lead a secret double life. Soaring higher than jumbo jets, they carry clues about disease spread and alien life.
articles.summary: Certain common Earth microbes soar higher than jumbo jets into the upper atmosphere. These high-flying germs help scientists study how diseases spread and what alien life might be like.
